claims.statement: ECHA describes SCIP as the database for substances of concern in articles and complex objects under the Waste Framework Directive.
The SCIP scope covers articles placed on the EU market containing Candidate List substances above 0.1% weight by weight.

ECHA's SCIP notification format models a recorded association between the duty holder and the article requiring notification, supporting a structured product/BOM workflow rather than a free-text filing.

contrary_evidence: The obligation applies only when Candidate List substances exceed 0.1% weight by weight in an article, so many products will not require notification.
ECHA operates the official database and data model, and companies can prepare submissions with existing ECHA/IUCLID tools.
ECHA reported dissemination delays from technical problems in 2026, showing that a private workflow cannot control official processing time.

economics.acquisition_route: Choose one component-rich vertical, partner with a REACH/SCIP consultancy, pilot on a permissioned BOM, and use a supplier-response portal as the expansion loop
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Unvalidated 5-8 year scenario: 100 manufacturers averaging 60,000 PLN annual revenue yields 6.0m PLN; at 32% EBITDA, 4x, and 70% ownership, equity value is about 5.38m PLN.
economics.founder_time: 18-24 hours per week with an external chemicals-compliance expert and narrowly scoped customer integrations
economics.gross_margin_basis: Candidate-list matching and reused component mappings are scalable; supplier chasing, lab testing, and ambiguous material declarations remain variable costs
economics.payback: Customer payback hypothesis: reusing supplier and component evidence across many products can remove hundreds of duplicate follow-ups and justify 40,000-120,000 PLN annually; test on a real BOM
economics.pricing: Unvalidated hypothesis: 15,000-50,000 PLN onboarding, 3,000-10,000 PLN monthly by BOM/supplier volume, and scoped data-cleaning projects
economics.retention_or_repeat: BOMs, suppliers, components, and the Candidate List change continuously; historical submissions and release decisions are difficult to reconstruct

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A permissioned graph of component-material-substance mappings and supplier response quality makes later products, changes, and Candidate List updates cheaper to assess
fingerprint.customer: Polish/EU machinery, electronics, furniture, automotive-component, and equipment SMEs placing complex articles on the EU market
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: REACH/SCIP consultants, testing laboratories, ERP/PLM implementers, contract manufacturers, and industry clusters
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Supplier declaration portal, BOM hierarchy, substance matching, uncertainty flags, release approval, SCIP dataset/export, and change impact alerts; hypothesis 15,000-50,000 PLN setup plus 3,000-10,000 PLN monthly
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Product compliance, engineering, or procurement lead pays implementation, annual BOM monitoring, and per-notification/product-family usage
fingerprint.problem_trigger: New product/BOM, supplier or material change, new Candidate List substance, customer declaration request, or SCIP submission failure

founder_fit: Uses entity resolution, graph modeling, data lineage, and automated change detection
High-value B2B niche can be reached through consultants rather than personal-brand marketing
Can start with synthetic and customer-permissioned BOM structures on a part-time basis
Connects to EU manufacturing and renewable-equipment supply chains without relying on employer assets
risks: Suppliers may not disclose adequate chemical information, leaving the platform unable to resolve obligations
Chemical and article-level interpretation errors can create regulatory liability
Established product-compliance, PLM, and supply-chain data networks already serve larger manufacturers
Security requirements are high because BOM and supplier data are commercially sensitive

structure.commercial_archetype: Supply-chain material declaration network with per-product compliance release and annual monitoring
structure.control_point: The BOM-level substance decision and SCIP notification evidence required to release an affected article or complex object to the EU market
structure.critical_dependency: Trustworthy supplier material declarations tied to exact component versions and maintained mapping to the changing ECHA Candidate List and SCIP data model

thesis: Planning-stage hypothesis: build a supplier-declaration and bill-of-materials evidence graph for EU manufacturers, importers, and assemblers of articles that may contain Candidate List substances above 0.1% by weight. The platform would collect supplier declarations, resolve article/complex-object hierarchies, map substances to current Candidate List entries, generate SCIP notification datasets, preserve submission evidence, and rerun impact analysis when the Candidate List or BOM changes. The internal product-release decision becomes the control point: an affected article cannot be approved until the required notification is prepared and evidenced. Supplier reliability and reusable component mappings could create a defensible data advantage.
title: SCIP BOM-to-Substance Notification Rail
uncertainties: Which SME vertical has enough BOM reuse and poor incumbent coverage
Supplier participation rate and acceptable declaration formats
Permitted submission methods and practical integration with ECHA/IUCLID tools
When laboratory testing is required and who bears that cost
